clue.text: Cambridge college admitting sons of old assassin

indicators.note: a college admitting people lets them in, so the college name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Gonville and Caius, usually just Caius, is a Cambridge college
S is the standard abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A historian notes which ancient Cambridge college took in the sons of an assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: Gonville and Caius is a Cambridge University college, pronounced 'keys', so the spelling surprises solvers who know it only by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaius Cassius Longinus was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar in 44 BC.

clue.text: Artist twice entering dock

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it, so the word for twice sits within the word for dock

parts.note: to dock a tail is to cut it
bis is Latin for twice, used in music and on addresses

explanation.surface: A painter appears twice in the dock, as if on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a courtroom or harbour, but here it is the verb for shortening a tail; 'entering' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of the Cubist school, such as Picasso or Braque, is a kind of artist.

clue.text: Maroon fibre

definitions.meaning: to maroon someone is to leave them stuck

explanation.surface: Maroon fibre reads as a dark red thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maroon' looks like the colour adjective, but it is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand means to leave helpless, as a castaway is marooned; a strand is also a thread.

clue.text: Starry-eyed setter visiting shop stocking article getting endless criticism

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: a shop stocking an item holds it inside, so the shop word contains the article

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop
A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed from the word for criticism

parts.note: stick means harsh criticism, as in taking stick

explanation.surface: A dreamy compiler drops into a shop and gets endless flak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' gives DEALI; 'endless' leaves STIC. 'visiting' and 'getting' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone starry-eyed is naively hopeful, holding lofty ideals rather than realistic views.

clue.text: Go away with stuff after start of sales

indicators.note: after places the word for stuff behind the opening letter
the start of a word is its first letter, here the opening of sales

parts.note: to cram is to stuff something full

explanation.surface: A shopper is told to leave after stuffing bags at the start of the sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command telling someone to leave at once.

clue.text: Foot of water in view

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to see is to view
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: A foot of water lies in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' means a metrical foot in poetry, not a body part or a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical unit in verse made of two stressed syllables.

clue.text: Snub involving head held up as focus of attention

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the word for snub wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a slight is a snub

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: top means the head of something

explanation.surface: A snub involving someone in charge is held up as the talk of the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss in the surface; 'held up' reverses its synonym, and 'involving' wraps the snub around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the spotlight means being the centre of public attention, like a stage lamp.

clue.text: Cook rabbit stuffed with vegetable

indicators.note: the words cook rabbit are stuffed with the answer, which lies concealed across them

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook a rabbit stuffed with a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'cook' and 'rabbit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called ladies' fingers, is a green pod eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Academic fighting to axe college's voluntary contribution?

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

indicators.note: to axe something is to cut it out, so the college letter is removed from the word for fighting

parts.note: action means fighting, as in soldiers seeing action
C is an abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A lecturer battles plans to shut a college, offering money?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to axe' removes C (college) from ACTION, leaving ATION. The question mark signals that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift freely given, such as money to a charity.

clue.text: Journalists welcoming time inside hollow monumental stones

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the word for journalists surrounds the rest

parts.note: eds is short for editors, the journalists who run a paper

indicators.note: the time word sits inside the remaining outer letters
hollow means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of monumental

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Reporters gather inside a hollow monument made of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' and 'inside' together make MERAL, which 'welcoming' places within the journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeralds are green precious gems, the stones set in jewellery.

clue.text: Rambert's head stopping basic support for dancers

indicators.note: a letter stopping a word plugs a gap in it, so it is placed inside

parts.note: bare means basic, as in the bare essentials

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here the opening of Rambert

explanation.surface: Rambert's director is blocking basic help for the company's dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambert is a well-known British dance company, which suits the ballet answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A barre is the horizontal handrail ballet dancers hold for balance during exercises.

clue.text: Ordering a suspect into river

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or unreliable, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone orders a suspect thrown into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun for a criminal; it is the anagram signal on ORDERING A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a major North American river forming part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: End-of-season game still cooked in booze

indicators.note: cooked means tampered with, as accounts can be cooked, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter, here the final one of season

explanation.surface: An end-of-season match is still being fixed by people in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: N, GAME and STILL are rearranged together; 'cooked' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A single malt is a Scotch whisky from one distillery, a kind of strong drink.

clue.text: Hot spot found over stake

indicators.note: over signals turning back, so the word for stake is read backwards

parts.note: an ante is the stake put into the pot in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler's lucky table turns up over a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna, in Sicily, is an active volcano, a literal hot spot spewing lava.

clue.text: Snake destroyed diarist's plant

parts.note: an asp is a small venomous snake

indicators.note: destroyed signals the letters of diarist are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A snake has wrecked a journal-keeper's favourite houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges DIARIST into IDISTRA; the 's reads as 'has' or as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, famously popular in Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Food for drab grooms wandering round Swedish capital

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the capital letter
wandering means roaming about, so the letters of drab grooms move out of order
the capital of a word is its first letter, here the opening of Swedish

explanation.surface: Dull bridegrooms wander about Stockholm in search of something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city such as Stockholm; it means the letter S. 'wandering' rearranges DRAB GROOMS, and 'round' wraps that about S.
explanation.definitionFit: A smorgasbord is a Swedish buffet spread of many hot and cold dishes.

clue.text: Rows erupting over a sultanate's athlete

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the mixed letters come before the sultanate
erupting means bursting out in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Disputes flare up over an Arabian state's sporting star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels (rhyming with 'cows'), but its letters are anagram fodder with A.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who rows competitively, as in a racing eight, is an athlete.

clue.text: Keep drug in cook's vessel

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep them for sale
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A chef is told to keep drugs hidden in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a large deep pan for simmering bones into broth.

clue.text: Fish eggs turned grey, reportedly

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word for eggs is read backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the colour word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: grey said out loud gives the American spelling of the same sound

explanation.surface: A fisherman finds the roe has gone grey, so he hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eggs' suggests fish roe, but it is NITS, louse eggs; 'turned' gives STIN. 'reportedly' gives GRAY, which sounds like grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea fish with a venomous barb on its tail.

clue.text: Voice disapproval about setter visiting France with Italian returning for ice cream

indicators.note: about means going around, so the disapproving sound surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: tut-tut is the noise made to express disapproval
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the abbreviation for Italian is read backwards

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A setter tuts at a trip to France with an Italian, then orders dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' splits the double tut after its fourth letter to take in the setter and France; 'returning' reverses the Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti-frutti is an ice cream containing chopped candied fruits.

clue.text: Plan made by spy without time to meet lawyer

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the time letter is taken out of the word for spy

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A scheme cooked up by a spy who has no time to see his attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes T from AGENT, leaving AGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule or programme.

clue.text: Spin tail of monkey in metal frame

indicators.note: in places the tail letter inside the frame word

parts.note: a grate is the iron frame holding fuel in a fireplace

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here the end of monkey

explanation.surface: A monkey's tail spins round inside a metal cage.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to rotate or whirl round a centre.

clue.text: Insincerity not working in part of Switzerland

indicators.note: not signals that the word for working is left out

parts.note: Switzerland is divided into regions called cantons
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Hypocrisy fails to function in a Swiss region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON from CANTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk, hence insincerity.

clue.text: Females given note in secret without a problem

indicators.note: the females and note go in the word for secret

parts.note: sly means secret or furtive, as on the sly
wimmin is a jocular or feminist spelling of women
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Women receive a note on the quiet without any trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'females' spelling is a deliberate respelling of women once favoured by some feminists; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Going swimmingly is an idiom for proceeding smoothly and easily.

clue.text: Locks guarding entrance to Scottish minister's residence

indicators.note: guarding means keeping safe within, so the locks word encloses the letter

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair, locks

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter, here the opening of Scottish

explanation.surface: Locks protect the way into a Scottish clergyman's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door security; here it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in the Church of Scotland.

clue.text: Pastrami sometimes contains paste used in Japanese cookery

indicators.note: contains means the answer is held within the run of clue letters

explanation.surface: Pastrami occasionally includes a Japanese cooking paste.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'pastrami' and the start of 'sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is fermented soybean paste, used in soups and sauces in Japan.

clue.text: One eating contents of pie with very little fruit

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the person word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a person is one individual

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, here the middle of pie

parts.note: mm, the millimetre, is a very small measurement

explanation.surface: Someone eats the filling of a pie with barely any fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is not the usual I here but a whole person; 'contents of' and 'eating' signal the selection and insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A persimmon is an orange tree fruit, also known as sharon fruit.

clue.text: Silver not returned to South Pacific kingdom

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver was never sent back to a Pacific island realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AGNOT around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian island nation ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Tony upset about haul that's worthless

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters surround the haul word
upset means knocked over, so the letters of Tony are disturbed

parts.note: to tow is to haul

explanation.surface: Tony is upset about a haul that proves worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives TOYN and 'about' wraps it around the haul word.
explanation.definitionFit: Toytown describes something trivial or petty, like a toy model of the real thing.

clue.text: Come out of aquatic mammal back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the final letter moves to the start

parts.note: a manatee is a sea cow, an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: Something emerges from a sea creature, back end first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the last E of MANATEE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.
